text:
SJS arrive at BOS on a high after a 6-2 win at OTT two days ago, part of a 3-1-1 stretch, though they are without Igor Chernyshov and Alexander Wennberg. Collin Graf has taken Wennberg's spot beside Marchment and Toffoli, and Alex Nedeljkovic starts over Yaroslav Askarov. BOS had Michael DiPietro stop all 28 shots in a 6-0 win over NSH, and they are 4-0-1 in their last five. These teams met Oct 13, when BOS won 6-3.

The chances favor BOS. At five on five, BOS has taken 53% of the expected goals (the quality of shots), against 45% for SJS, whose defense allows 3.90 expected goals per 60 minutes. BOS's results run ahead of its chances, with finishing and goaltending doing the lifting. BOS has also taken 4.3 penalties a game, which keeps feeding power plays. Projected goalies: Nedeljkovic is +4.6 in goals saved above expected this season after -2.1 over 40 games last year. Jeremy Swayman is +7.7 after +26.5 last year.

Macklin Celebrini, the 2024 first overall pick, is 43% to score and 81% for a point. David Pastrnak is 34% to score. Our under-the-radar picks are both BOS: James Hagens, a third-liner with 2.7 expected goals in his last 10 games, and JJ Peterka, 51% for a point because SJS give up so many chances. Both are players to watch, not locks.
